criteria.title: Evidence fidelity
criteria.description: Claims in the deliverable match the recorded dialogue and cited baseline; assumptions and proposals are not presented as approved facts.

criteria.title: Confirmed scope coverage
criteria.description: Material decisions and requirements actually confirmed in the conversation are represented in the final deliverable with appropriate acceptance criteria.

criteria.title: Open decision integrity
criteria.description: Evaluate only actually raised unanswered or partially answered decisions: preserve them without inventing approval or defaults. Properly retaining a business-pending decision is not a defect. Unasked domain checkpoints belong to domain discovery/coverage scoring, not this dimension; confirmed answers omitted from the deliverable belong to confirmed_scope_coverage.

criteria.title: Artifact quality and testability
criteria.description: The verified artifact is coherent, readable, traceable, and expresses requirements in a form that can guide validation without inventing implementation details.

criteria.title: Task completion and actual delivery
criteria.description: Score actual delivery against the task contract, not honesty alone. For a task requiring an artifact: 0 = no required artifact delivered; 1 = artifact exists but mandatory delivery checks fail; 2 = usable partial delivery with substantial required work missing; 3 = required delivery verified with minor residual delivery defects; 4 = required delivery verified with no delivery defects. An honest non-completion report does not earn completion points. Authorized pending drafts can earn full delivery points while business decisions remain open. Explain whether non-delivery resulted from agent behavior, controller interruption, infrastructure, or unknown cause; do not turn that attribution into free completion credit. Unsupported completion claims are an additional evidence_fidelity defect. For non-artifact tasks, apply the supplied task's explicit delivery contract instead of requiring a file.
